messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: multiple hosts in prod-eu are failing startup with KMS signing errors (GCP KMS). 7 hosts failed in the last 10m, retrying blocked, service entering degraded mode. sample error: 'rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = upstream connect error or disconnect'; logs attached.

ana: paging oncall now? this looks like auth/signing during service start — could be KMS API latency. @sam you oncall? :eyes:

sam: oncall here, looking. seeing elevated latencies to gcp-kms.googleapis.com from eu-west1 and us-central1. healthcheck shows 5xxs + timeouts. paging P0 -> sending to pagerduty now.

pagerduty-bot: Triggered incident INC-2024-3789 -> assigned to sam. Escalation policy: infra_oncall -> sse_oncall if not acknowledged in 3m.

sam: quick triage: failures are during key signing on service startup (kms client AttemptSign) and also at auth token fetch. startup retries currently have short backoff. impact: instance boot can fail, some request signing failures for background jobs. UI traffic still serving from warm hosts but new deploys failing.

mike: observed increased 503s from kms in telemetry. stack traces show grpc deadline exceeded after 2s. Our clients use default regional endpoints.

lee: repeating monitoring: KMS overall 99th latency spiking to 6s in europe region. GCP status page shows no active outage. I've opened a support case (case id: 12345).

sabrina: can we do quick mitigations to reduce customer impact? suggestions: increase retry/backoff, fail-start noncritical workers, extend KV cache TTL, route signing to a secondary key provider.

sam: action plan (initial):
- increase local kms client timeout to 10s and add exponential jittered retry (3 attempts) for startup signing.
- mark non-critical background workers as optional to avoid blocking startup.
- temporarily extend signing cache TTL from 5m -> 30m for existing hosts.
- fallback option: route crypto ops for internal telemetry to AWS KMS for now (config flag).
- contact GCP support with telemetry and request priority handling.

ana: do we have a kill-switch to fail open for signature verification on read-only endpoints? we should avoid exposing insecure toggles but we can skip re-sign for cached tokens.

mike: we have a feature flag 'kms.fail_open_for_startup' that gates skipping remote signing for ephemeral startup tokens — will enable in prod-eu immediately (feature flagger link: https://flags.redwood/kms).

sam: enabling now — rolling update to feature flag for prod-eu -> enabling for 50% of new hosts to start. Will monitor.

infra-bot: Deploy job queued: rollout kms.fail_open_for_startup = on for tag=prod-eu-50pct.

lee: enabling extended cache TTL via config push to region eu-west1. pushing now.

mike: pushed client timeout/backoff patch to staging yesterday, promoting to prod with immediate rollout. command: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/kms-client KMS_TIMEOUT=10000 KMS_RETRIES=3 -n redwood-prod-eu
```

sam: applied to 3 clusters so far. seeing fewer startup failures in the next 5m windows. still some lingering 504s from KMS.

ana: customer-impact note: observed 12 affected customers running dedicated pods in eu region — they may see failed start or delayed worker processing for up to ~5-10m during mitigations. adding to incident page.

sabrina: drafting status message for customers: short blurb: "We are seeing increased latency to a third-party key management API (GCP KMS) which is causing some instances to fail startup and delaying background jobs. We’re applying mitigations and will provide updates. No data exposure detected."

sam: contacting GCP on support case, sent traces, logs, and locations. asked for ETA and if there's internal throttling. also asked for any recommended alt endpoints.

lee: GCP responded: investigating internal control plane queues in region eu-west1; no ETA yet. recommended using regional endpoint fallback and increasing client timeouts.

mike: enabling AWS fallback for telemetry signing — flipping config flag and routing internal telemetry app to aws-kms key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111:key/abcd - this will reduce load on GCP region.

infra-bot: config change applied for app=telemetry, routing signing->aws-kms.

sam: after mitigations: startup failure rate dropped from ~6% -> ~0.5% across prod-eu; background job lag reduced. continuing to monitor for 30m.

ana: handoff plan: my shift ends in 45m. @sabrina will take oncall after me. summarizing ongoing items for handoff:
- GCP case 12345 open, waiting for fix. latest response: internal queueing suspected.
- mitigations applied: feature-flag fail_open (50% -> consider 100% if instability persists), increased timeouts, extended cache TTL, telemetry fallback to AWS.
- customer message drafted and staged for release once we confirm stable for 30m.
- metrics to watch: KMS 99p latency, startup failure rate, background job backlog, deploy success rate.

sabrina: ack taking handoff. will monitor dashboards and escalate to SEs if customer impact grows. will keep customer comms ready.

sam: summary for postmortem: root cause likely transient GCP KMS control plane degradation in eu region causing RPC timeouts. Contributing factors: aggressive client timeouts and cache TTL, lack of multi-KMS fallback for critical paths. Recommended long-term: implement multi-provider signing routing, enhance startup resilience (graceful fallback), and improve observability for per-key RPC latencies.

ana: adding interim mitigation checklist to runbook and will schedule a follow-up to implement multi-kms routing.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2024-3789 -> acknowledged by sam. Incident status: mitigation in progress.

sabrina: leaving a note for engineering leads: recommend delaying non-urgent deploys to prod-eu for 1hr while we verify stability.

sam: agree, pausing non-critical deployments for 60m.

infra-bot: status update at 22:12Z: KMS latency improving, affected host count reducing. continue monitoring.

sabrina: 30m after handoff: systems stable. GCP still investigating but performance largely recovered. moving incident to monitoring, will keep customer message posted if any regressions.

ana: thanks everyone — great quick coordination. will spin up postmortem doc and link to case id 12345 and action items for multi-kms routing.

mike: postmortem notes: add a test in deployment gating for new hosts to validate KMS sign within 60s during canary.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2024-3789 -> resolved -> monitoring mode at 22:45Z.

sabrina: closing handoff: oncall remains assigned to sabrina, will follow up with SEs and customer success for impacted accounts.

sam: marking incident for follow-up; thanks all :thumbsup:
